title: The right proper Kan-Quillen model structure
statement: On the category of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] let $\Delta^n$ be the representable $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$, let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of its proper faces, and for $n\geq1$ let $\Lambda_i^n$ be the union of all faces except the $i$th, $0\leq i\leq n$. A weak homotopy equivalence is a map whose geometric realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms of all homotopy groups at all basepoints. There is a functorial model structure with these weak equivalences, degreewise injective maps as cofibrations, and maps with the right lifting property against every $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ as fibrations (Kan fibrations). Its fibrant objects are the Kan complexes. A map is a trivial fibration exactly when it has the right lifting property against every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Every monomorphism is a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of boundary inclusions. Trivial cofibrations are the retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions. Pullback of any weak homotopy equivalence along any Kan fibration is a weak homotopy equivalence (right properness). A homotopy pullback of a cospan of Kan complexes is represented by replacing one leg by a weak equivalence followed by a fibration, and then taking the ordinary pullback. The resulting space is independent, up to natural equivalence, of this replacement.
